precepts.point: Job says his righteousness he holds fast and will not let it go, and his heart shall not reproach him so long as he lives, saying he is not a hypocrite; what he says, he does.

note.label: Job 27: I Will Not Remove My Integrity From Me

precepts.why:
Job says, “till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.” Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles: moral uprightness, honesty, good character, righteousness, doing what is right even when no one is looking.

Someone is always looking: “The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.” Even when you think nobody is watching, he sees. Job kept the commandments to the best of his ability because he loves the Lord and fears the Lord; he did what he was supposed to do when nobody was watching, not just getting in order when the righteous come around or when he feared correction from men.

It is like the ring of Gyges in Plato's Republic, a ring that turns you invisible. The question of ethics is whether you still do the right thing and uphold your integrity, or go against everything you learned in uprightness. You do good whether you are invisible or not, faithful to the Most High and keeping his laws at all times, because his eyes are in every place.

precepts.text: The integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them; walking upright is integrity even when nobody is watching.
precepts.point: Job says his righteousness he holds fast and will not let it go, and his heart shall not reproach him so long as he lives, saying he is not a hypocrite; what he says, he does.

note.label: Job 27: I Will Not Remove My Integrity From Me

precepts.why:
“The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” Job says, “My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.” He is not a hypocrite; what he says, he does.

Walking upright is integrity even when nobody is watching, and that integrity guides a man. The perverse transgressor, who only gets in order when the righteous come around, is destroyed by his own perverseness. Job holds his integrity till he dies, and it guides him through everything he is going through.

note.label: Job 27: I Will Not Remove My Integrity From Me

precepts.why:
“Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep.” Those that remain are those left after the Most High brings the bombs: “And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.”

Flesh consuming away while men stand on their feet is the ICBM, the intercontinental ballistic missile, the nukes. This is the portion of a wicked man with God and the heritage of oppressors, their due reward for their works: Esau, Moab, the Amorites, Ammonites, Jebusites, Hittites, and the Negroites in these last days that come against Israel, and also the wicked of our own people, who get no pass just because they come from the seed of Isaac, Abraham, and Jacob. If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword.

precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” Those left are those left from the bombs, the ones Job calls “Those that remain of him”.

So feast days are kept in the kingdom. Everyone left of the nations goes up year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and keep the feast of tabernacles. “And it shall be, that whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain.”
